description: How many agents a role may have running at once, and how many a session may run in total. Spawn authority answers whether a role may delegate; this answers how much. Without it, a role permitted to spawn thirteen kinds of agent may spawn thirteen agents for a one-line change.
why: An agent-team member or subagent is a full Claude session. A feature that fans out to a director, three architects, five developers, four QA and three security roles is sixteen sessions, and nothing in the spawn hierarchy prevents that for a typo fix.

The limit escalates rather than denies. A wide fan-out is sometimes correct, and the person running the session is the one who can tell. What must not happen is that it occurs without anyone choosing it.
Concurrency is measured, not declared. hooks/lib/ledger.py records each allowed spawn and clears it when the work ends.

session_limit.why: Across every role in one session. Ten concurrent agents is already an unusual amount of parallel work.

engineering-director.why: Forms cross-functional teams, so it legitimately fans out widest. Six is a large team by any human standard.

incident-commander.why: An incident wants parallel investigation, but an incident that needs more than four simultaneous investigators needs a second commander, not a bigger one.

development-lead.why: One worker per parallel stream. More streams than this in a single stage usually means the stories were not decomposed.

qa-lead.why: Test execution parallelises; test design does not.

product-manager.why: Requirements and UX work in parallel. Nothing else.

security-architect.why: Security review and dependency review together.

ledger.why: An entry older than this is treated as finished whether or not a stop signal arrived. The hook cannot always correlate a subagent's end with its start, and a limit that leaks slots would eventually block all delegation. Erring toward forgetting is right: this is a guardrail against runaway fan-out, not an exact semaphore, and a stuck slot is worse than a missed one.

limitations: Teammate spawns that Claude Code performs outside the Agent tool are not counted; the hook never sees them.
The count is per session. Two sessions doing the same work do not see each other.
A subagent that ends without any stop signal holds its slot until the TTL expires.

A spawn with no session id is not counted and not limited. There would be no boundary to count within: every caller would share one ledger, and unrelated work would contend for the same slots. A limit that cannot be scoped correctly is not applied.
